clue.text: Foreign food briefly available in this Aegean island

indicators.note: briefly asks for the food's name cut short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a samosa is a fried Indian pastry, a food of foreign origin

explanation.surface: A tourist notes that some exotic snack can be bought on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' removes the last A of SAMOSA; 'available in this' just links the food to the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island lying in the eastern part of that sea, near Turkey.

clue.text: Takes away inferior publications?

parts.note: sub- means below or lesser, as in substandard
tracts are short published pamphlets

explanation.surface: Someone removes second-rate magazines from the shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take one quantity away from another, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A boy follows lead of master craftsman

indicators.note: follows means these pieces come after the master's first letter
the lead of a word is its first letter, at the front

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An apprentice lad walks behind the master of his trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a skilled worker in stone, a traditional craftsman.

clue.text: Opening of swish eatery on former platform

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café
old means former, as in an old flame

explanation.surface: A smart restaurant has opened on a site that used to be a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: CAFF is informal British English for a basic café, the opposite of 'swish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, especially one used for executions or building work.

clue.text: Having broken loose, criminal eluded cop

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are behaving wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker escaped a policeman and got free.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoupled means separated or disconnected, as something that has come loose from what held it.

clue.text: Exclude delivery

definitions.meaning: to leave out someone from a team, as when a player is axed
a consignment set down at a place, as in a parcel or supply handover

explanation.definitionFit: To drop a player is to exclude them, and a drop is a delivery of goods or supplies.

clue.text: Take a new direction, getting cash on the nail

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, places the cash above the nail

parts.note: change is loose cash in coins
a tack is a small nail

explanation.surface: A trader is paid immediately ('on the nail') and decides to go another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the nail' is a British idiom for paying at once, which hides the plain reading of nail as TACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To change tack is a sailing idiom for altering one's course or approach.

clue.text: Promote university head about end of semester

indicators.note: about means the head word goes around the next letter

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A college principal is advanced around the close of term.
explanation.definitionFit: To uprate is to raise to a higher grade, much like promoting someone.

clue.text: Avoiding drink, tucks into endless amounts of food late at night

indicators.note: tucks into means one piece is pushed inside another
endless asks for the final letter to be dropped

parts.note: lashings are generous helpings of food, a British usage
TT means teetotal, someone who avoids alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A teetotaller wolfs down huge helpings at a midnight feast.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is a crossword staple for someone who avoids alcohol; 'Avoiding drink' looks like advice rather than a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Last thing is an idiom for the final moment of the day, typically before bed.

clue.text: Charge raised after introduction of new currency

indicators.note: after introduction of means the next letter is put into the reversed charge
raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attacking charge

explanation.surface: A fee went up when a fresh monetary unit came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RAID into DIAR; N goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is a monetary unit used in several countries such as Kuwait and Serbia.

clue.text: Eggs on master, note, after a dance

indicators.note: after means the note comes behind the a
on means the eggs are added to the end of what precedes

parts.note: a boss is a master or employer
ova are eggs, the Latin plural

explanation.surface: Someone urges on their employer, makes a note, and then dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as urging, but the eggs are OVA tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style derived from samba.

clue.text: Rinse out sticky stuff

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of place, rearranged

explanation.surface: Wash away the gummy residue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance secreted by plants such as pine trees.

clue.text: Escape further contest

definitions.meaning: an extra deciding round after a tie

explanation.definitionFit: To run off is to escape, and a run-off is a deciding contest held after a tie.

clue.text: It is eaten by a Florida reptile, one causing disturbance

indicators.note: is eaten by means the first word goes inside the creature

parts.note: gator is short for alligator, common in Florida

explanation.surface: An alligator in Florida swallows something, then turns troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up public unrest, a person who causes disturbance.

clue.text: Look for something to say

definitions.meaning: a look on someone's face, such as a frown
a phrase or idiom one might utter

explanation.definitionFit: An expression is both a facial look and a phrase or saying used in speech.

clue.text: Meet specified standards installing door? It's far from straightforward

indicators.note: installing means one word is fitted inside the other

parts.note: to comply is to meet set rules or standards
an exit is a door out

explanation.surface: Bringing a door up to regulations turns out to be complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Complexity is intricacy, the quality of something being complicated rather than simple.

clue.text: Swell party at home -—- your setter's brought round something to eat

indicators.note: brought round means the setter's word is put around the other pieces

parts.note: your setter refers to the person writing the clue, giving me
ace and swell both mean excellent
a do is a party
in means at home

explanation.surface: The setter brings food to a great party held at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your setter's' is ME, the clue writer; the 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A macédoine is a mixture of diced fruit or vegetables, a dish to eat.

clue.text: Post a large amount of money

definitions.meaning: a heavy upright beam driven into the ground
a fortune, as in making one's ...

explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a post driven into the ground, and informally a fortune, as in making a pile.

clue.text: English politician, one ready to reorganise old May holiday

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to reorganise means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An English MP is keen to reform an old spring holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Empire Day was a British celebration held on 24 May, Queen Victoria's birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: Empire Day was a former British Empire holiday held each May.

clue.text: Leave, having made one's point?

parts.note: after scoring a point in argument, or with a pencil, one retreats; the question mark flags the play on making a point and drawing back

explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to leave or retreat from a place or discussion.

clue.text: It carries coal for fire

definitions.meaning: a bag used for carrying coal

explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a bag for carrying coal, and to sack someone is to fire them.

clue.text: Laughing out loud when having a breakdown?

explanation.definitionFit: Cracking up means both laughing uncontrollably and suffering a mental collapse.

clue.text: Bomber, soaring up, identified old man's address

indicators.note: soaring up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Bomber Harris was the RAF wartime commander of Bomber Command

explanation.surface: A warplane climbing has been spotted, as an old man speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur 'Bomber' Harris led RAF Bomber Command in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirrah is an archaic form of address to a man or boy, often contemptuous.

clue.text: Most finicky girl gets weaker, going without nourishment finally

indicators.note: going without means the weakening word goes outside the girl

parts.note: fades means grows weaker
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The fussiest girl grows feeble from refusing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' reads as fasting, but means FADES goes outside DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddy means fussy about food, so the faddiest is the most finicky.

clue.text: Lots to be said for such gala events

indicators.note: to be said means the word is spoken and heard

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: Plenty is spoken in favour of summer galas.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetes are outdoor fund-raising fairs, festive gala occasions.

clue.text: Huntsman needed one drink after another

definitions.meaning: a drink taken after another, as a beer after a whisky

explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is one who chases, as in a hunt, and a drink taken after another.

clue.text: Sensible to skirt round river in France

indicators.note: to skirt means the sensible word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a sensible person is of sound mind, rational
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: It is wise to go round a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saône is a river of eastern France, a tributary of the Rhône.

clue.text: Revolutionary curtailed an expression of delight

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a wheel revolves, so it is a revolutionary thing

explanation.surface: A rebel was cut short in his cry of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a rebel but means something that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: Whee is an exclamation of excitement or delight.

clue.text: Judge a town in Germany

explanation.definitionFit: A trier is one who tries cases, a judge, and Trier is a German city on the Moselle.

clue.text: Writer is joining crowd round court

indicators.note: joining means the first piece is attached to what follows
round means the crowd word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a herd is a crowd
to woo is to court

explanation.surface: An author joins a throng gathered round a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Woman in shape, surprisingly, after consuming most of meal

indicators.note: consuming means the scrambled letters take in the next piece
surprisingly means the letters come out in an unexpected order
most of drops the last letter

parts.note: tea is a meal

explanation.surface: A woman is surprisingly fit after eating nearly all her dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the woman, but it belongs to the anagram fodder along with 'shape'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephanie is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Small and extremely dainty quite unlike Charles Atlas

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: extremely picks out the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tiny, delicate figure is nothing like the famous strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Atlas was a famous bodybuilder who advertised courses for skinny weaklings.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy means thin and feeble, the opposite of a muscular bodybuilder.
